newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total Gonfreville refinery slows output due strike.
newsitem.headline: Total Gonfreville refinery slows output due strike.

text.p: A group of workers at Total SA's 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gonfreville refinery in Normandy joined a one-day strike on Tuesday, forcing the plant to operate below its normal rate, a company spokesman said.
Information on two other Total refineries, where unions have called a strike for midday, was not yet available, he said.
"At the Normandy refinery there is a minority on strike and this has caused some decline in production," he said.
Unions have called a one-day strike across the oil industry for Tuesday to protest against job cuts. But so far only a minority of France's 13 refineries is scheduled to take part.

The Communist-backed CGT union, leading the protest alongside the CFDT and three other unions, said disruption was scheduled at two BP refineries, Dunkirk and Lavera, and the Esso plant at Fos in southern France. There was no immediate confirmation from the companies, although an employee at Lavera said a strike was happening.
Workers at the Royal Dutch/Shell Berre refinery extended a strike begun on Monday for another 24 hours from early Tuesday morning, a plant official said.
The CFDT union said a go-slow was also planned at Shell's 140,000 bpd Petit Couronne refinery.
A Shell France spokeswoman said any action was planned for around midday and there was no information so far.
